page.title: Start Work Request
page.subtitle: Create a tracked work request that Work OS can route, monitor, and follow through to completion.
page.description: This page is for normal users, team members, and operators who need to start new work from chat, email, a form, a webhook, or a manual request.
page.forUsersBody: Use this page when you want to start a new request, ask for help, or hand a task to the operations team.
page.forAdminsBody: After a request is created, the Work OS Console can route it, reassign it, attach legacy tasks, and review the full case timeline.
form.title: Title
form.titlePlaceholder: Example: Review refund request for Order #1842
form.detailsPlaceholder: Add context, desired outcome, blockers, or any links that help the team act faster.
form.sourceType: How did this work come in?
form.sourceRefPlaceholder: Example: chat thread ID, webhook event ID, ticket number
form.ownerIdPlaceholder: Example: support-queue, finance-review, or team queue ID
recent.title: My recent requests
recent.subtitle: These are the requests you created most recently.
recent.empty: You have not created any work requests yet.
success.title: Work request created
success.body: Your request is now tracked and ready for routing or follow-up.
list.title: My Requests
list.subtitle: Track the work you started and see what happens next.
list.description: This page helps you review requests you created, see who owns them now, and jump back into Work Request when you need to start more work.
list.emptyBody: Start a new request and it will appear here.
helper.title: What happens next
helper.step1: A request record is created first, then a case is opened for tracking.
helper.step2: If a team or queue should own it, the case can be assigned after creation.
helper.step3: Admins can review approvals, exceptions, SLA changes, and the case timeline in Work OS Console.
